Clinton-Jackman-Rivers Bayesian IRT

Source: R/svb.R
cjrirt.Rd

The probit ideal-point model \(P(y_{ij} = 1) = \Phi(\beta_j' x_i - \alpha_j)\) with priors \(x_i \sim N(0, I)\) and \((\alpha_j, \beta_j) \sim N(0, v I)\) (Clinton, Jackman and Rivers 2004), by the Gibbs sampler of Albert and Chib (1993): latent utilities from truncated normals, then every \((\alpha_j, \beta_j)\) and every \(x_i\) from its normal full conditional. Every draw is an inverse normal of a uniform of Philox4x32-10 (Salmon et al. 2011), sweep \(t\) on stream \(t\) of key seed, so a chain is the same on every platform. The default start is the posterior mode of irtem().

Usage

cjrirt(
  votes,
  ndim = 1,
  nsamp = 1000,
  burn = 200,
  bvar = 25,
  start = NULL,
  seed = 0,
  chains = TRUE
)

Arguments

votes

A legislator-by-vote matrix: 1 yea, 0 nay, NA absent.

ndim

The number of dimensions; ndim times the points scaled must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

nsamp

The draws kept; nsamp times the values kept per draw must be at most 67108864 (2^26).

burn

The sweeps discarded first; burn plus nsamp must be at most 2147483647.

bvar

The prior variance \(v\) of the vote parameters.

start

NULL, or starting ideal points.

seed

The Philox key, a whole number from 0.

chains

Whether to return the draws as well.

Value

A list of class cjrirt: ideal, sd, alpha, beta, nsamp and, with chains, xchain (draws by legislators by dimensions), achain and bchain.

References

Clinton, J., Jackman, S. and Rivers, D. (2004). The statistical analysis of roll call data. American Political Science Review, 98(2), 355-370. doi:10.1017/S0003055404001194

Albert, J. H. and Chib, S. (1993). Bayesian analysis of binary and polychotomous response data. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 88(422), 669-679. doi:10.1080/01621459.1993.10476321

Salmon, J. K., Moraes, M. A., Dror, R. O. and Shaw, D. E. (2011). Parallel random numbers: as easy as 1, 2, 3. Proceedings of the International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis (SC11). doi:10.1145/2063384.2063405

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr(), wrdfsh()

Examples

votes <- rbind(c(1, 1, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 1, 1, 1),
               c(0, 0, 1, 1), c(1, 0, 0, 0))
round(cjrirt(votes, nsamp = 50, burn = 10)$ideal, 3)
#>        [,1]
#> [1,] -1.209
#> [2,] -0.508
#> [3,]  0.358
#> [4,]  0.859
#> [5,] -0.904
